html:
In 1584 and 1585 a Spanish army under Alexander Farnese, Duke of Parma, besieged and took Antwerp, then the richest trading city in northern Europe, which had joined the Dutch revolt.

Parma cut the city off from the sea by building a bridge of boats across the Scheldt. The defenders sent fire ships packed with explosives against it, but the city surrendered in August 1585. Protestants were given time to leave, and tens of thousands did, many of them merchants and craftsmen.

The Dutch rebels then closed the Scheldt to shipping, which they kept shut for two centuries. Antwerp declined, and its people and money moved north, helping make Amsterdam the new centre of world trade. The fall fixed the split between the Spanish south, later Belgium, and the Dutch north in the Eighty Years' War. It ended the age of Antwerp at the centre.
sum: In 1584 and 1585 a Spanish army under Alexander Farnese, Duke of Parma, besieged and took Antwerp, then the richest trading city in northern Europe, which had joined the Dutch revolt.
